State Implementation Plan (Air Quality)
SEMRPC is currently integrating the abatement, prevention and control of air pollution on a regional basis with the region's long-range transportation and land use plans. To accomplish this, the Misconsin Department of Transportation, Department of Natural Resources and SEMRPC are now participating in study to produce a regional air quality maintenance plan. It is anticipated that the plan will be completed by December, 1975 with a formal report published by July 1, 1976 which is in accordance with the latest EPA regulations. This plan would coordinate all emissions sources, ambient air quality monitoring efforts and air pollution control activities within the region with regional plans of land use changes and transportation developments.
According to DNR the Regional Transportation Plan as prepared by SEWRPC is consistent with the State Implementation Plan as it presently exists, prior to its current revisions which have yet to be finalized. Federal regulations now require certification that these transportation plans are consistent with Wisconsin's State Implementation Plan for attaining national ambient air quality standards.
According to SENRPC, their studies completed to date indicates that the elimination of automobile congestion through highway construction is an effective means of reducing the total emissions of carbon monoxide and hydrocarbons with the region.
